Hello,

I am trying calculating residuals from a multiple-QTL fit. I think I found a way in a case of only additive QTLs, but I'd rather have your back-up on that.
In the pure additive case, I calculate the theoretical phenotype value of individuals as :
Y= I + A((G-2)/2) + D(G==2)
with
I= intercept
G = genotype of the individual at the QTLs
I took the genotypes at the closest marker so far, because I don't know how to deal with probabilities of genotypes at the QTL positions. I don't think it's too much of a problem in my case because the genotyping is reasonably dense.
A = vector of a effect values at the QTLs
D= vector of the d values at the QTLs

I should precise I am working with an F2 population.

Is it correct?

In addition, I don't really understand how to put the effects of the interaction between two QTLs into the equation. The help of fitqtl indicates: "Epistatic effects and QTL x covariate interaction effects are obtained through the products of the corresponding additive/dominant effect columns." I am afraid I don't quite understand.  In the effects table fitqtl provides values that look like interaction effects but I don't know how to use them.
Can you help me on this point?

Thank you very much !
Françoise

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How do I calculate residuals after fitQTL ?
parts:
In an intercross, the additive effect covariate is coded as -1, 0, 1 for AA, AB, BB genotypes. So that's (G-2) rather than (G-2)/2.
The dominance effect is -0.5, +0.5, -0.5, and so should be (G==2)-1/2.

This is where it happens in the fitqtl code: https://github.com/kbroman/qtl/blob/master/R/fitqtl.R#L481-L491

If you have two QTL and you're including their interaction, then in the X matrix for the regression, you'd multiply each of the two columns for the first QTL with each of the two columns for the second QTL, to create four additional columns to add to the X matrix.

I think what I should do, at least for method="hk" and model="normal", is to just return the residuals from the fit.

regards,
karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: How do I calculate residuals after fitQTL ?
parts:
I think I've been able to get fitqtl to return the residuals. Download and install the development version, 1.32-1, from http://www.rqtl.org/download/devel

Here's an example:

  data(fake.f2)
  fake.f2 <- calc.genoprob(fake.f2, step=1)
  qtl <- makeqtl(fake.f2, c(1, 13), c(27, 28), what="prob")
  outfq <- fitqtl(fake.f2, qtl=qtl, method="hk")
  res <- attr(outfq, "residuals")
  fit <- fake.f2$pheno[,1] - res
  plot(fit, res)

karl

I think I've been able to get fitqtl to return the residuals. Download and install the development version, 1.32-1, from http://www.rqtl.org/download/devel

Here's an example:

data(fake.f2)
fake.f2 <- calc.genoprob(fake.f2, step=1)
qtl <- makeqtl(fake.f2, c(1, 13), c(27, 28), what="prob")
outfq <- fitqtl(fake.f2, qtl=qtl, method="hk")
res <- attr(outfq, "residuals")

plot(fit, res)

karl

I think I've been able to get fitqtl to return the residuals. Download and install the development version, 1.32-1, fromhttp://www.rqtl.org/download/devel

Here's an example:

data(fake.f2)
fake.f2 <- calc.genoprob(fake.f2, step=1)
qtl <- makeqtl(fake.f2, c(1, 13), c(27, 28), what="prob")
outfq <- fitqtl(fake.f2, qtl=qtl, method="hk")
res <- attr(outfq, "residuals")
fit <- fake.f2$pheno[,1] - res
plot(fit, res)

karl
